two decades of inflation in one line what the cpi tells us about the economy brookstone news jan 25 2026 if you want to understand the economic story of the past twenty years you could do worse than look at a single line the chart below from the us bureau of labor statistics tracks the 12month percentage change in the consumer price index cpi from 2005 through the end of 2025 its a clean time series of all items inflation not seasonally adjusted and it quietly captures three major economic eras the financial crisis the pandemic shock and the long struggle back toward price stability the calm before the storms from 2005 through 2007 inflation mostly hovered between 2 and 4 this was the final stretch of the great moderation when price stability was taken for granted and central banking seemed boring then came the first gray band on the chart the global financial crisis inflation collapsed sharply in 20082009 briefly turning negative as demand cratered oil prices plunged and deflation fears spread it was one of the few times in modern us history when falling prices not rising ones were the central concern a decade of low and stable inflation what followed was an unusually quiet period from roughly 2010 through 2019 inflation rarely strayed far from 13 even as unemployment fell to historic lows prices refused to accelerate central bankers worried more about inflation being too low than too high this long stretch anchored expectations households firms and policymakers came to believe that inflation around 2 was simply the natural state of the world then came the second gray band the pandemic shock and the inflation surge the pandemic recession in 2020 initially pushed inflation down again but the recovery that followed rewrote the playbook by 2021 and especially 2022 inflation exploded upward peaking near 9 the highest rate in four decades supply chains snapped energy prices surged fiscal stimulus flooded the economy and demand roared back faster than production could keep up the red line on the chart climbs almost vertically this was not a gentle overshoot it was a regime break disinflation but not a full return to normal since that peak inflation has come down dramatically by late 2023 and through 2024 the line descends steadily by december 2025 inflation sits around 23 far below the crisis highs and close to where it stood before
